Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings  
• Acute dysuria, suprapubic discomfort, malodorous urine, and single episode of hematuria without systemic features (fever, flank pain).  
• Sexually active with new partner; no prior STI screen.  
• No significant past medical issues except IBS; allergy to clindamycin (angioedema).  

Working diagnosis  
• Uncomplicated acute cystitis (bacterial UTI) – high likelihood based on classic symptom triad and absence of systemic signs (supported by DDx).

Considerations  
• Chlamydial/gonococcal urethritis or cervicitis – medium likelihood; recommend STI screening.  
• Distal urolithiasis – low to medium likelihood; consider if hematuria persists or pain localizes.  

Management  
• Empiric antibiotics: nitrofurantoin or trimethoprim 1 tablet BID × 3 days (avoid clindamycin due to allergy).  
• Hydration advice; consider cranberry products.  
• Abstain from sexual activity until symptoms resolve; continue condom use thereafter.  
• Safety-net: return or call if persistent symptoms after antibiotics, development of fever, flank/back pain, or systemic illness (possible pyelonephritis).  
• Offer pregnancy test to definitively exclude early pregnancy.  
• Discuss and arrange first STI screen (Chlamydia, Gonorrhea, others as per guidelines).

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

1. Uncomplicated acute cystitis – High likelihood: acute dysuria, suprapubic pain, malodorous urine, hematuria, typical demographic, no systemic signs.  
2. Chlamydial/gonococcal urethritis or cervicitis – Medium likelihood: new sexual partner, no prior STI screen, dysuria may be urethral.  
3. Distal urolithiasis – Low-Medium likelihood: hematuria with dysuria, but absence of colicky flank pain makes less likely.
